Article 11

The family in efforts to protect women's rights is responsible for:
a. Protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;
b. Providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural, and
c. Preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

PROTECTION

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Payakumbuh.
2. Regional Government is the Government of the City of Payakumbuh.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Payakumbuh.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit within the Government of the City of Payakumbuh.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of protective, preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) measures.
6. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
7. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and Parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
8. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
9. Child-Friendly Regency/City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights;
10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb'
11. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
12. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
13. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
14. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
15. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families and the community.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
20. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims;
21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence;
22. Transit house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
23. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
24. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
21. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
26. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
27. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from generation to generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns.

Article 41

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, family, community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. Directly.
b. By telephone; and
c. By letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 43, are also authorized to handle victims of violence against women and children obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 45

1. Health services for women and children victims of violence are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
2. Health services for women and children victims of violence are carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and carried out in accordance with health service standards.
3. Health services specifically for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.
4. Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. Medical services
b. Medicolegal services
c. Psychosocial counseling.
5. Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (4) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER XI

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 59

1. Guidance for the implementation of protection of women and children is carried out by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (i) may be carried out in the form of;
a. Providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence.
b. Providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children.
c. Providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at Community Health Centers, integrated service units and General Hospitals.
d. Providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence, and
e. Conducting professional improvement of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.

Article 50

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 48

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women and child victims of violence.
2. Safe houses aim to protect women and child victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators and other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for women and child victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. Their life is threatened;
b. Receiving rejection from family or community;
c. Requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. Abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
5. The provision of safe house services is carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of:
a. Social workers;
b. Volunteers;
c. Security officers and
d. Community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 49

1. Women and child victims of violence are provided with spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.
2. Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. Not imposing any religion and belief; and
b. Leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
3. Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
4. Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of Consultants of the Marriage Advisory, Development and Preservation Agency (BP4), Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA), Ustads/Ulamas, Priests, Pastors and other gender-responsive religious leaders.

Article 15

1. In the context of preventing violations against children's rights, parents or guardians:
a. Provide good examples to children in accordance with religious and customary teachings;
b. Supervise children in their activities inside or outside the home;
c. Provide opportunities for children to dialogue and express opinions democratically; and
d. Protect children from various acts of violation of children's rights in the household.
2. In the context of preventing violations against women's rights, the family:
a. Protects women from various violations of rights in the household; and
b. Encourages the formation of a harmonious, educative and democratic family.

Article 42

The implementation of handling women and children victims of violence includes:
a. Handling complaints of victims of violence.
b. Health services
c. Social rehabilitation
d. Law enforcement and legal assistance, and
e. Repatriation and social reintegration.

Article 51

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing assistance and protection to women and child victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.
2. Types of legal aid services include:
a. Legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of BAP.
b. Legal aid in the prosecution process at the Prosecutor's Office.
c. Legal aid in the examination process at the Court.
d. Legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. Legal aid in the Mediation process.
f. Legal aid in the Diversion process.
3. The Regional Government provides legal aid to children and women victims of violence.
4. In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with Legal Aid Institutions (LBH), Women Crisis Centre (WCC), Advocates and/or other gender-responsive legal assistants.

Article 52

1. Repatriation of victims of violence is aimed at returning women and child victims of violence to their area of origin;
2. Repatriation of women and child victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regional Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and child victims of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 46

1. Social Rehabilitation Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence are aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of victims who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social Rehabilitation Services as referred to in paragraph (1) include counseling services, provision of safe houses and spiritual guidance.
3. The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:
a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social sector.
b. SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
c. Handling service institutions.

Article 43

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Point b What is meant by Non-Discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.

Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in the provision of services. Officers must convey this principle to victims Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any way.

Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be judged or condemned.

Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that the provision of services must be done with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken. Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language that is understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and other backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Lately there are more and more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that the provision of services must be given immediately without unnecessary delay. Perhaps some interventions require various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Point k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the convention on the rights of the children. Convention on the elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women (convention on the elimination of All Against Women)

Article 25

Children in formal and non-formal educational institutions must be protected from acts of violence.

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor and rights as human beings that must be upheld. The human rights of children are part of human rights included in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and from acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the dignity of women themselves, women and children often become objects, outlets for desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support is needed, laws and regulations that can guarantee its implementation.

The Convention on the Rights of the Child (Child Rights Convention) affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the government established Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the Rights of the Child, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government and the State. Child protection in all its aspects is part of National development activities, especially in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, family and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

Although the protection and rights of women and children have been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Payakumbuh City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children.

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing assistance and protection to women and child victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.
2. Types of legal aid services include:
a. Legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of BAP.
b. Legal aid in the prosecution process at the Prosecutor's Office.
c. Legal aid in the examination process at the Court.
d. Legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and

4. In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with Legal Aid Institutions (LBH), Women Crisis Centre (WCC), Advocates and/or other gender-responsive legal assistants.

Article 10

1. The responsibilities of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. Participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. Provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. Monitor the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama, cadiak pandai and bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. The responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on laws and regulations and local wisdom values of the local community.

6. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

8. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
9. Child-Friendly Regency/City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights;
10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb'
11. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
12. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
13. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
14. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence;
22. Transit house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.

21. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

2. Health services for women and children victims of violence are carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and carried out in accordance with health service standards.
3. Health services specifically for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.

b. Medicolegal services
c. Psychosocial counseling.

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor and rights as human beings that must be upheld. The human rights of children are part of human rights included in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and from acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the dignity of women themselves, women and children often become objects, outlets for desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support is needed, laws and regulations that can guarantee its implementation.

The Convention on the Rights of the Child (Child Rights Convention) affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the government established Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the Rights of the Child, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government and the State. Child protection in all its aspects is part of National development activities, especially in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, family and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

Although the protection and rights of women and children have been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Payakumbuh City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children.

7. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and Parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
8. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
9. Child-Friendly Regency/City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights;
10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb'
11. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
12. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
13. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
14. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
15. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families and the community.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
20. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims;
21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence;
22. Transit house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
23. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
24. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
21. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
26. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor and rights as human beings that must be upheld. The human rights of children are part of human rights included in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and from acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the dignity of women themselves, women and children often become objects, outlets for desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support is needed, laws and regulations that can guarantee its implementation.

The Convention on the Rights of the Child (Child Rights Convention) affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the government established Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the Rights of the Child, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government and the State. Child protection in all its aspects is part of National development activities, especially in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, family and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

Although the protection and rights of women and children have been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Payakumbuh City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children.

d. Protect children from various acts of violation of children's rights in the household.

a. Protects women from various violations of rights in the household; and
b. Encourages the formation of a harmonious, educative and democratic family.

1. Everyone is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.

a. All work in the form of slavery or similar practices.
b. All work that exploits, provides or offers children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances or gambling.
c. All work that exploits, provides, or involves children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances and/or
d. All work that endangers the health, safety and morals of children.

a. serve as a guideline for the Regional Government in planning, policies and strategies for the protection of women and children.
b. protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate the rights of women and children.
c. prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
d. increase empowerment of women.
e. increase the role and value of local wisdom and the role of customs in the protection of women and children, and
f. increase the role of government and non-government institutions in efforts to protect women and children.

12. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
13. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
14. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
15. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families and the community.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
20. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims;
21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence;
22. Transit house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
23. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
24. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
21. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
26. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
27. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from generation to generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns.

Article 45

1. Health services for women and children victims of violence are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
2. Health services for women and children victims of violence are carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and carried out in accordance with health service standards.
3. Health services specifically for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.
4. Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. Medical services
b. Medicolegal services
c. Psychosocial counseling.
5. Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (4) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 41

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, family, community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. Directly.
b. By telephone; and
c. By letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 43, are also authorized to handle victims of violence against women and children obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 49

1. Women and child victims of violence are provided with spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.
2. Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. Not imposing any religion and belief; and
b. Leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
3. Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
4. Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of Consultants of the Marriage Advisory, Development and Preservation Agency (BP4), Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA), Ustads/Ulamas, Priests, Pastors and other gender-responsive religious leaders.

Article 3

The regulation of protection of women and children aims to:
a. serve as a guideline for the Regional Government in planning, policies and strategies for the protection of women and children.
b. protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate the rights of women and children.
c. prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
d. increase empowerment of women.
e. increase the role and value of local wisdom and the role of customs in the protection of women and children, and
f. increase the role of government and non-government institutions in efforts to protect women and children.

Article 48

2. Safe houses aim to protect women and child victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators and other parties.

4. Criteria for women and child victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. Their life is threatened;
b. Receiving rejection from family or community;
c. Requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. Abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

a. Social workers;
b. Volunteers;
c. Security officers and
d. Community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 42

The implementation of handling women and children victims of violence includes:
a. Handling complaints of victims of violence.
b. Health services
c. Social rehabilitation
d. Law enforcement and legal assistance, and
e. Repatriation and social reintegration.

Article 43

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Point b What is meant by Non-Discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.

Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in the provision of services. Officers must convey this principle to victims Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any way.

Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be judged or condemned.

Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that the provision of services must be done with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken. Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language that is understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and other backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Lately there are more and more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that the provision of services must be given immediately without unnecessary delay. Perhaps some interventions require various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Point k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the convention on the rights of the children. Paragraph 2

Responsibilities for the Protection of Children

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor and rights as human beings that must be upheld. The human rights of children are part of human rights included in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and from acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the dignity of women themselves, women and children often become objects, outlets for desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support is needed, laws and regulations that can guarantee its implementation.

The Convention on the Rights of the Child (Child Rights Convention) affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the government established Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the Rights of the Child, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government and the State. Child protection in all its aspects is part of National development activities, especially in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, family and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

Although the protection and rights of women and children have been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Payakumbuh City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children.

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor and rights as human beings that must be upheld. The human rights of children are part of human rights included in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and from acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the dignity of women themselves, women and children often become objects, outlets for desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support is needed, laws and regulations that can guarantee its implementation.

The Convention on the Rights of the Child (Child Rights Convention) affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the government established Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the Rights of the Child, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government and the State. Child protection in all its aspects is part of National development activities, especially in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, family and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

Although the protection and rights of women and children have been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Payakumbuh City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children.

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Point b What is meant by Non-Discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.

Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in the provision of services. Officers must convey this principle to victims Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any way.

Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be judged or condemned.

Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that the provision of services must be done with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken. Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language that is understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and other backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Lately there are more and more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that the provision of services must be given immediately without unnecessary delay. Perhaps some interventions require various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Point k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the convention on the rights of the children. Part One

Handling of Women and Children Victims of Violence

Article 43

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Point b What is meant by Non-Discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.

Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in the provision of services. Officers must convey this principle to victims Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any way.

Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be judged or condemned.

Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that the provision of services must be done with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken. Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language that is understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and other backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Lately there are more and more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that the provision of services must be given immediately without unnecessary delay. Perhaps some interventions require various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Point k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the convention on the rights of the children. I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor and rights as human beings that must be upheld. The human rights of children are part of human rights included in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and from acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the dignity of women themselves, women and children often become objects, outlets for desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support is needed, laws and regulations that can guarantee its implementation.

The Convention on the Rights of the Child (Child Rights Convention) affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the government established Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the Rights of the Child, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government and the State. Child protection in all its aspects is part of National development activities, especially in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, family and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

Although the protection and rights of women and children have been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Payakumbuh City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children.

6. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

8. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
9. Child-Friendly Regency/City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights;
10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb'
11. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
12. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
13. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
14. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

22. Transit house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.

21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence;

Article 48

Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of protective, preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) measures.
6. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

8. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
9. 14. 22. Transit house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.

24. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
21. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
26. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
27. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from generation to generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns.

Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of protective, preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) measures.

21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence;
22. Transit house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.

21. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of protective, preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) measures.
6. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
9. 13. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
14. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

17. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.

21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence;
22. 21. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

CHAPTER VII

HANDLING AND SERVICES

Part One

Handling of Women and Children Victims of Violence

Article 42

The implementation of handling women and children victims of violence includes:
a. Handling complaints of victims of violence.
b. Health services
c. Social rehabilitation
d. Law enforcement and legal assistance, and
e. Repatriation and social reintegration.

Article 51

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing assistance and protection to women and child victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.
2. Types of legal aid services include:
a. Legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of BAP.
b. Legal aid in the prosecution process at the Prosecutor's Office.
c. Legal aid in the examination process at the Court.
d. Legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. Legal aid in the Mediation process.
f. Legal aid in the Diversion process.
3. The Regional Government provides legal aid to children and women victims of violence.
4. In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with Legal Aid Institutions (LBH), Women Crisis Centre (WCC), Advocates and/or other gender-responsive legal assistants.

Article 49

1. Women and child victims of violence are provided with spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.
2. Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. Not imposing any religion and belief; and
b. Leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
3. Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
4. Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of Consultants of the Marriage Advisory, Development and Preservation Agency (BP4), Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA), Ustads/Ulamas, Priests, Pastors and other gender-responsive religious leaders.

Article 48

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women and child victims of violence.
2. Safe houses aim to protect women and child victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators and other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for women and child victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. Their life is threatened;
b. Receiving rejection from family or community;
c. Requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. Abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
5. The provision of safe house services is carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of:
a. Social workers;
b. Volunteers;
c. Security officers and
d. Community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER XI

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 59

1. Guidance for the implementation of protection of women and children is carried out by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (i) may be carried out in the form of;
a. Providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence.
b. Providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children.
c. Providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at Community Health Centers, integrated service units and General Hospitals.
d. Providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence, and
e. Conducting professional improvement of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.

Article 50

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 52

1. Repatriation of victims of violence is aimed at returning women and child victims of violence to their area of origin;
2. Repatriation of women and child victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regional Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and child victims of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 45

1. Health services for women and children victims of violence are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
2. Health services for women and children victims of violence are carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and carried out in accordance with health service standards.
3. Health services specifically for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.
4. Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. Medical services
b. Medicolegal services
c. Psychosocial counseling.
5. Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (4) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 23

Paragraph (1) What is meant by women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability is an adult woman, married, unmarried or widowed and does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
